claims.text: Co-alloying a high-entropy alloy with molybdenum and sulfur in suitable amounts will form MoS2-based lubricious phases in situ.
Approximately 10 wt% MoS2 equivalent is a potentially sufficient addition level for improved tribological behavior.
MoS2-containing high-entropy-alloy bulk materials can be produced using powder metallurgy and spark plasma sintering.
Sliding will generate an MoS2-rich tribofilm at the interface of the Mo-S-doped alloy.
Molybdenum and sulfur react during frictional contact to produce MoS2-based solid lubricant.
A dichalcogenide-based lubricant can exhibit self-lubricating behavior associated with stress-induced tribocatalytic activity during sliding.
MoS2-based lubricious material lowers interfacial shear strength and therefore lowers the coefficient of friction.
The MoS2-based tribofilm protects the alloy matrix specifically from abrasive wear.
Adding Mo-S-derived lubricious material will lower both friction and wear relative to an untreated high-entropy alloy.
The reductions in friction and wear will remain consistent from room temperature to approximately 800 °C.
The untreated high-entropy alloy has a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.6–0.8.
Mo-S doping will decrease friction by 30–50% relative to the untreated alloy.
Mo-S doping will reduce wear rate by at least a factor of two relative to the untreated alloy.
The intervention should remain effective under moderate to high contact loads.
The intervention should remain effective in both air and controlled-inert environments.
Above approximately 800 °C, the protective MoS2 film may degrade and lose effectiveness.
Excessively high load or highly reactive conditions may degrade the protective film and reduce its effectiveness.
The untreated alloy has higher friction and wear because it lacks a lubricious tribofilm.
